To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Se-hormetic drug, 2,2’-diselenyldibenzic acid (DSB) protects bone marrow hematopoeitic cells from radiation damage by activating the Nrf2 pathway.

DSBA is a Se-hormetic molecule that protects bone marrow hematopoeitic cells from ionizing radiation-induced damage by activating the Nrf2 signaling pathway in both bone marrow hematopoetic cells and liver tissue.
DSBA is a seleno-homeric compound which protects hematopoietic tissues against ionizing radiation induced damages by inducing Nrf2 pathway.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and characterization of novel Se-hormetic agents with potential pharmacological applications.
the identification of new seleno-compound-based drugs with hormetic activity that may be used to protect tissues against stress conditions.
the discovery of novel seleno-homertic compounds with potential applications in the prevention and/or treatment of human pathologies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the present study demonstrated that the Se-hormetic molecule DSBA, in addition to its previously demonstrated anti-cancer properties, is a radioprotector that may be useful in cancer treatments and/or as a preventive agent against the toxic effects of ionizing radiation.
DSBA is a Se-hormetic molecule that protects hematopoietic tissues against the toxicities caused by exposure to ionizing radiation.
DSBA has the potential to be developed as a radioprotection agent for use during radiotherapy and/or chemotherapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the seleno-homoretic molecule DSBA is a potent radioprotectant, which acts via Nrf2 pathway in hematopoietic and liver cells.
DSBA is a novel radioprotective agent that protects bone marrow cells from radiation-induced toxicities by enhancing Nrf2-dependent antioxidant response.
Se-hormetic compounds may have potential as radioprotectives and/or prevention agents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
seleno-homertic compounds can be used as a novel type of agents to prevent the toxicities of ionizing radiation in the treatment of cancer patients.
the Nrf2 pathway is a potential pharmacological target in cancer prevention and therapy.
DSBA is a promising candidate as a radioprotection and/or prevention agent for use in the clinic.
